chapter: Joining Raeburn and work for other leaders
title: Boyd's reaction, and the band's manager Lou
summary: Boyd let the new music happen while knowing little; the manager Lou also went along.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: (Side B of Tape 2 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Tape 3.)
I think they were probably a little surprised; they were. But they were pleased. Everybody was delighted.
It wasn't a particularly difficult chart, you didn't have an awful lot of trouble running it down.
No. I didn't feel that anything was difficult.
What did Boyd think about it?
What could he do? He looked at the expression on the guys' faces and they looked happy; he looked happy. He didn't know.

Boyd--I don't know what justification, other than business, he would have for being an orchestra leader. He was a piss poor musician with not even good taste. I think he went along with everything that was done because
people who he thought knew what was going on dug it. Boyd was number one opportunist; he was smart in that way.
I'm sure he knew he had something; he didn't know what it was, but something was happening right in front of his eyes and he wasn't going to stop it. He let it happen.
Who was managing the band at that point?
At that point there was a guy named Lou--what was his last name--he had a daughter who became a popular singer. I can't think of his last name--Lou something.

He didn't know either, but he also went along with it. They noticed that people were starting to come to our rehearsals, our rehearsals began to look like performances, there were so many people around.
